claims.text: Untreated HfZrTiTa0.53 has a yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
Untreated HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
Untreated HfZrTiTa0.53 has a terminal strain of approximately 13.5%.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has limited tensile ductility and uniform elongation.
The proposed intervention is deep cryogenic treatment at approximately -196 °C for 24–48 hours.
Deep cryogenic treatment will improve the tensile ductility and uniform elongation of HfZrTiTa0.53.
Deep cryogenic treatment will induce a beneficial secondary-phase or martensitic transformation in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Deep cryogenic treatment will increase lattice distortion in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Deep cryogenic treatment will reduce residual stresses in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Cryogenic cooling reorganizes defects and activates additional slip systems, increasing dislocation-motion paths during tensile loading.
Deep cryogenic treatment will increase uniform elongation by at least 15–20% relative to untreated HfZrTiTa0.53.
After deep cryogenic treatment, the yield strength of HfZrTiTa0.53 will remain at or above 786 MPa.
After deep cryogenic treatment, the compressive strength of HfZrTiTa0.53 will remain near 1314 MPa.
After deep cryogenic treatment, impact-triggered chemical-energy release will be comparable to or greater than that of untreated HfZrTiTa0.53.
The predicted ductility benefit applies at room temperature under quasi-static tensile loading at approximately 10^-3 s^-1.
The effects of deep cryogenic treatment may differ at elevated temperatures or very high strain rates.
Untreated HfZrTiTa0.53 has demonstrated impact-triggered energy release.
In Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr, deep cryogenic treatment increased tensile strength by 25% relative to as-cast material and by 11% relative to as-deposited material.
In Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr, deep cryogenic treatment increased elongation by 48% relative to as-cast material and by 10% relative to as-deposited material.
Deep cryogenic treatment induced a phase transition in Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr without additional deformation.
